title: Zoology

events.title: Bubalus Period
events.text: 12000–8000 BC. Bubalus Period creation of rock art in the Central Sahara depicting a range of animals including elephants, antelopes, rhinoceros and catfish.

events.title: Xenophanes

events.title: Lucius Annaeus Seneca
events.text: 50. Lucius Annaeus Seneca (Roman, 4 BC–65 AD), tutor to Roman emperor Nero, maintained that animals have no reason, just instinct, a "stoic" position.

events.title: Thomas of Cantimpré

events.title: Conrad Gessner

events.title: Captain John Smith

events.title: Marcello Malpighi

events.title: Maria Sybilla Merian
events.text: 1705. Maria Sybilla Merian (German, 1647–1717) wrote and illustrated her ' (') (1705). In this book she stated that Fulgora lanternaria was luminous.

events.title: British Museum
events.text: 1753. The British Museum was founded in the will of Sir Hans Sloane (English (born Ireland), 1660–1753). It would open its doors in 1759.

events.title: Antoine Lavoisier
events.text: 1780. Antoine Lavoisier (French, 1743–1794) and Pierre Laplace (French, 1749–1827) wrote Memoir on heat. Lavoisier, the discoverer of oxygen, concluded that animal respiration was a form of combustion.

events.title: Lazaro Spallanzani
events.text: 1793. Lazaro Spallanzani (Italian, 1729–1799) conducted experiments on the orientation of bats and owls in the dark.

events.title: Alexander von Humboldt
events.text: 1803. Alexander von Humboldt (German, 1769–1859) and Aimé Jacques Alexandre Goujaud Bonpland (French) arrived in Venezuela in 1799. Humboldt's Personal Narrative of Travels to the Equinoctial Regions of America during the years 1799–1804 and Kosmos w

events.title: Malayan tapir
events.text: 1819. Malayan tapir, a first species of tapir to be discovered, is described.

events.title: James Smithson
events.text: 1829. James Smithson (English, 1765–1829) donates seed money in his will for the founding of the Smithsonian Institution in Washington.

events.title: Louis Agassiz
events.text: 1839. Louis Agassiz (Swiss-American, 1807–1873), an expert on fossil fishes, founds the Museum of Comparative Zoology at Harvard University, and becomes Darwin's North American opposition. He was a popularizer of natural history. His ' (1842–1847) wa

events.title: Josiah C. Nott
events.text: 1848. Josiah C. Nott (American), a physician from New Orleans, publishes his belief that mosquitoes transmit malaria.

events.title: Gregor Mendel
events.text: 1865. Gregor Mendel demonstrates in pea plants that inheritance follows definite rules. The Principle of Segregation states that each organism has two genes per trait, which segregate when the organism makes eggs or sperm. The Principle of Independen

events.title: Polypodium hydriforme
events.text: 1885. Polypodium hydriforme, an unusual cnidarian, is described.

events.title: Okapi
events.text: 1901. Okapi is described for science.

events.title: Prague Zoo
events.text: 1931. Founding of Prague Zoo.

events.title: developmental biologists
events.text: 1952. American developmental biologists Robert Briggs and Thomas King clone the first vertebrate by transplanting nuclei from leopard frog embryos into enucleated eggs.

events.title: John Gurdon
events.text: 1967. John Gurdon used nuclear transplantation to clone an African clawed frog; first cloning of a vertebrate using a nucleus from a fully differentiated adult cell.

events.title: Dian Fossey
events.text: 1985. The primatologist Dian Fossey is murdered by poachers.

events.title: insect
events.text: 2002. First species from insect suborder Mantophasmatodea are described.

events.title: Halicephalobus mephisto
events.text: 2011. Halicephalobus mephisto, a species of nematode living 3.6 km under the surface of Earth in gold mines in South Africa, is discovered.

events.title: Eumillipes persephone
events.text: 2021. Eumillipes persephone, a species of millipede with up to 1,306 legs and the first myriapod known to have more than 1,000 legs is discovered.
